THE MILITARY FAMILY, 3 OF ~10: THE LAST REPORT. A unit held the site and stopped reporting. Read what they left
in two places, in any order, deal with whoever holds it now, and take the unit's tags out of the room where it
ended. The verb is READ: the story is in the objects, and the radio only asks.
The two logs never say first or last (an any-order group), and neither depends on the other.
Written to the delve marker set (item markers 01 to 03, boss), so the lint pool is EMPTY on military sites until
he adds the markers (missionboard06a's note says why). Pay: med on the tags.

CARD 2026-11-10 (his 11-04 ruling, a posting by whoever set the job: no payer label, no payment line; his 11-10 'we still have all those X Contract things'). Was: "Private Contract. Find out what happened to the unit at the <Place> on <Planet> and recover their tags. Payment on contract completion."

place._theme: Military sites; the family's marker set.

prose.name: Recovery: Last Report on <Planet>
prose.briefing: A unit was holding the <Place> and stopped reporting twelve days ago. Their records office wants to know what happened, and wants their tags back.
prose.card: Our unit at the <Place> stopped reporting twelve days ago. We want to know what happened, and we want their tags back.

beats.objective: Find out what happened to the unit

message.title: Unit Field Terminal
message.text: The last entries are a supply request, sent four times, each one shorter than the one before.

beats.journal: The unit's field terminal. The last entries are a supply request, sent four times, each one shorter than the one before.
beats.name: Unit Field Terminal

message.title: Unit Footlocker
message.text: A roster taped inside the lid. Six names, five of them crossed out in the same pen, neatly.

beats.journal: A footlocker with a roster taped inside the lid. Six names, five of them crossed out in the same pen, neatly.
beats.name: Unit Footlocker

beats.objective: Deal with whoever holds the <Place> now
beats.journal: I've cleared the people who moved into the <Place> after the unit. Now I need to find their tags, which should be close.
say: You've found them. Bring the tags home.

beats.journal: A unit at the <Place> stopped reporting after their supplies never came. I read what they left, cleared the people squatting there, and recovered all six of their tags.
beats.name: Sealed Case

message.title: Unit Tags
message.text: Six sets of tags on one chain, in a case shut with a twist of wire. The sixth set is on the outside of the bundle.

say: All six. I'll tell the families myself, before anyone else does.

broadcast: We lost contact with that unit twelve days ago, and nobody's been out since. I need to know what happened, and I need them home.
_speech: On a board the broadcast waits for him at the site. Voice 'Brian, Deep, Resonant and Comforting', unused so far; his ear decides. No names, places, factions or currency.
